frameforge_implications: [INFERENCE] Preserve per-source evidence roles and dates when merging this supplement with the October 20 baseline. The catalog contains 30 official URLs: 14 inherited references and 16 directly read supplemental sources.
limitations: Inherited references lack individual publication/update dates and detailed extracted source claims. Null dates are intentional. Baseline adoption decisions are FrameForge decisions, not proof of Adobe behavior. The old project-templates URL returned HTTP 404; research used the documented current create-your-own-project-templates URL instead. Search summaries incorrectly described September features as October releases; only directly read official release dates were retained. The backward-compatibility page's v15.x examples remain stale despite its 2026 update timestamp.

observed_facts: CURRENT DOCUMENTATION: A project records sequences, assets, settings and edits non-destructively; export encodes a new file rather than altering source files. Adobe recommends matching sequence/timeline version numbers with exported file version numbers for reliable feedback cross-reference.

CURRENT DOCUMENTATION: Multiple projects can remain open. Window > Projects lists open projects and their associated panels. Dragging media or sequences between ordinary open projects copies the elements rather than moving/removing the originals.

CURRENT DOCUMENTATION: Team Projects store/manage the project in the cloud and share updates. Productions divide a larger work into smaller projects; collaborators need access to the same media. Productions support source clips in one media project referenced by sequences in other projects, without creating corresponding duplicate source clips in each timeline project. This referencing model is specific to Productions, not standalone projects.

CURRENT DOCUMENTATION: In a Production, clip markers propagate when source and sequence projects are both open read/write; a sequence-only marker created without source write access synchronizes when both projects later become read/write. Label colors are different: after insertion into a sequence, their values become independent of the source and other instances.

CURRENT DOCUMENTATION: Custom workspaces can be saved and explicitly selected while switching projects, then reset to their saved layouts. This documents layout continuity, not a guarantee of complete selection/playhead persistence.

CURRENT DOCUMENTATION: Standalone projects retain current media path plus two historical paths; Team Projects retain current and unlimited historical paths. Fallback automatic search checks the project folder/subfolders and then its parent, with Link Media for unresolved files. Cross-platform continuity depends on consistent folder structure. Adobe advises consistent mapped drive letters for Windows network collaborators and keeping media outside the Production folder containing the .prodset file.

CURRENT DOCUMENTATION: After a crash, Reopen restores available projects to their pre-crash state; saving a restored project writes to the main file. Dismissing the restoration prompt prevents its reappearance on the next launch. File > Revert returns to the last user-saved state; timestamped Auto-Save or Recovery Projects versions can be opened manually.

IN-WINDOW, PRE-BASELINE CHANGES: April 2026 version 26.2 documented improved relinking; June version 26.3 documented automatic Object Mask restoration when moving projects between systems. September version 26.5 fixed moved-clip cross-project references, newer-version Production handling and several relink failures. Version 26.5.2 fixed concurrent NAS Production save/move/rename problems. These changes were documented before October 20, not newly released during the supplement interval.
frameforge_implications: [INFERENCE] Give production, source asset, sequence/output variant, workflow run and exported artifact separate stable identities. Preserve the active production and selected asset/run across research, edit, graph, review and delivery surfaces rather than reconstructing context from labels.
[INFERENCE] Define which data is shared, copied or instance-local. Shared source identity must not imply that every label, template override or approval automatically propagates.

[INFERENCE] Show explicit missing-media and recovery states, version compatibility and read-only ownership; do not silently replace a production or reset the current selection when references cannot resolve.
limitations: [uncertain] Exact selection, playhead and inspector persistence across project switching, application relaunch, and every surface is not established by these documents and was not runtime tested.

Compatibility is not universally guaranteed: the general backward-compatibility page still illustrates v15.x, while the specific December 19, 2025 notice documents a 25.6.0 file-format exception within 25.x. Do not extrapolate a blanket same-major or 26.x downgrade guarantee. No conversion utility was downloaded or installed.
Relinking is not content-hash identity, provenance verification, or rights clearance. Renamed media, substantially changed folder structures and unmounted drives can require manual intervention.

observed_facts: NOT APPLICABLE to the scoped comparison: Premiere's project/sequence editing model is not the node-based production execution graph being compared for FrameForge. The inherited baseline explicitly did not implement arbitrary stage types, conditional scheduling or new skip/bypass semantics.

No claims are made about typed workflow node ports, saved node execution logs, cancellation semantics, partial retry, or artifact-level reuse in Premiere. Encoder handoff is an inherited export reference, not evidence of those execution contracts.
frameforge_implications: [INFERENCE] Reuse the visual editing shell without pretending the timeline is an execution graph. Keep run status, evidence, cancel/retry and reusable output identity explicit in FrameForge's own workflow model.
limitations: This is an applicability boundary, not a product-wide claim that no Adobe feature or extension can execute a graph. Node-engine research was outside this supplement.

observed_facts: CURRENT DOCUMENTATION: Premiere links media and uses media-path history to recover access; project edits are non-destructive. A file path or successfully relinked clip establishes a technical reference, not its creator, authenticity or reuse license.

CURRENT DOCUMENTATION: Adobe's project-template guide lists logos, graphics and organization-licensed Adobe Stock elements as reusable template content. It does not state that copying a project grants new rights to the incorporated media.
NOT APPLICABLE within this scoped supplement: stock search/download/provider licensing research belongs to the separate footage-source research. No footage was acquired, licensed or downloaded.
frameforge_implications: [INFERENCE] Preserve original provider URL, provider asset ID, retrieval record, license/attribution evidence and derivative constraints independently of local paths, proxy files and project membership. Require explicit clearance before reuse across channels.
limitations: [uncertain] Machine-readable rights persistence, original source-URL retention, attribution enforcement and redistribution permission across Premiere project/template copies are not established by this scoped evidence. Public visibility, authentic origin and reuse permission must remain separate checks.

observed_facts: HISTORICAL BASELINE, October 20: The supplied artifact lists official documentation for workspaces, docking, panel navigation, Source/Program monitors, timeline navigation and Properties. Its adopted FrameForge choices include project bin and monitor-over-timeline layout, selection-driven existing inspector, real workflow history/review navigation and responsive native controls/focus preservation. These are inherited design decisions, not fresh Adobe runtime observations.

CURRENT CONTINUITY GAP: Window > Projects lists open projects and associated panels; workspace saving/selection is documented for multiple open projects. This extends project continuity only; the general layout, docking, monitor, timeline and Properties research was not repeated.

CHANGE CHECK: The current release pages establish no post-October-20 workspace change. Earlier version 26.5 notes mention Selection Follows Playhead, and version 26.5.2 fixes keyboard-adjusted Effect Controls values not being retained. These are pre-baseline releases, not new four-day changes.
frameforge_implications: [INFERENCE] Keep one production workspace with a persistent project/asset bin, preview, real sequence or stage representation, selection-driven inspector and run/review result views. Switching task surfaces should not require inventing another production instance or discarding selection.
[INFERENCE] Offer explicit project/run selectors and saved view layouts; distinguish workspace restoration from persisted production data and live execution state.
limitations: [uncertain] The inherited artifact contains a bibliography and adoption summary, not detailed extracted docking/focus rules or proof of complete production-state restoration. No before/after UI comparison, responsive breakpoint testing or application observation was performed; unchanged behavior since October 20 cannot be guaranteed.

observed_facts: CURRENT DOCUMENTATION: A reusable project can contain bins, search bins, timeline layouts, track names, labels, effects, prebuilt sequences, editable titles, logos, music, graphics and compositions. Adobe's prescribed template workflow makes a named copy on the media drive and adapts it for the new project. This is copied project configuration, not documentation of a live-linked channel definition or immutable version pin.

CURRENT DOCUMENTATION: A Motion Graphics template is added from Graphics Templates > My Templates to a sequence track; selecting the timeline instance exposes author-provided controls in Properties. Available options can include colors, source text, animation, fonts and font sizes. Only parameters offered by the template's author are guaranteed editable; the guide also describes trimming instance duration.

CURRENT DOCUMENTATION: Media Replacement applies only when the template provides it. Specified placeholder images, video backgrounds and logos can be swapped while retaining design/animation structure.

CURRENT DOCUMENTATION: Source Graphics are explicitly shared: editing text, style or content in one instance affects every instance of the same Source Graphic, including the original upgraded graphic. This behavior must not be confused with independent project-template copies or assumed for every MOGRT.

CURRENT DOCUMENTATION: Auto Reframe Sequence creates a duplicate sequence at the selected preset/custom aspect ratio, optionally custom width/height, and applies Auto Reframe to every clip. The duplicate lives in Auto Reframe Sequences at the Project panel root. Motion tracking offers Slower Motion, Default and Faster Motion. Optional nesting preserves complex motion/speed changes and leaves graphics/audio unaffected, but nesting does not properly retain soft transitions because handle media is absent. Complex action can require manual keyframe refinement.

IN-WINDOW, PRE-BASELINE CONTEXT: June 2026 release notes describe single-word captions for social platforms; September Match Source adds audio channel/sample-rate adaptation with downmixing and unsupported-layout warnings. These are documented output-adaptation features, not channel-account or credential isolation features.
frameforge_implications: [INFERENCE] Define a reusable template separately from a production instance, pin a template revision on instance creation, and expose typed text/color/media/aspect/caption/audio parameters rather than copying opaque whole-project state.

[INFERENCE] Make update semantics visible: independent copied instance, explicit revision upgrade, or intentionally shared linked resource. Linked brand graphics should warn about their propagation scope.

[INFERENCE] Model channel branding defaults and target-specific output variants separately from channel publishing accounts and secret credentials. Parameter reuse should not copy credentials or silently switch destinations.
[INFERENCE] Preserve the original sequence and lineage when creating portrait/square variants, and require human review of framing, captions, transition handles and audio adaptation before delivery.
limitations: [uncertain] An immutable MOGRT version pin, automatic propagation of changes to installed template files, channel-specific default inheritance, and cross-channel credential/permission isolation are not established by these documents. Channel semantics are a FrameForge design inference, not a native Premiere template contract.

Aspect-ratio duplication is not guaranteed semantic adaptation: graphics placement, rapid action, text-safe areas and nested transitions can still need review. A documentation update date is not a feature introduction date.

observed_facts: HISTORICAL BASELINE, October 20: The artifact already catalogs export video/options/settings, Media Encoder handoff, Frame.io review and comments. It explicitly lists automatic external publication and Frame.io integration as not implemented in the recorded FrameForge work. These inherited topics were not re-researched.

CURRENT CONTINUITY GAP: Adobe recommends keeping sequence version numbers synchronized with exported file versions. Its template guidance recommends duplicating a sequence for export and naming the export copy so it can be found in an Exported Sequences search bin. These are documented organization practices, not cryptographic approval binding or automatic approval invalidation.

CURRENT DOCUMENTATION: Project edits do not mutate source files; export generates a new encoded artifact. A project version, exported file, shared review object and published channel item should not be treated as the same identity.
frameforge_implications: [INFERENCE] Bind approval to the exact production revision and exported artifact identity; mark it stale after material edits or replacement exports. Keep render, export, review sharing, upload, processing and publication separate states.

[INFERENCE] Before upload, display the resolved channel/account, destination and visibility, enforce permissions, and retain provider post-action read-back tied to the approved artifact. Do not infer success from an encoder job or review link.
limitations: [uncertain] Exact artifact-approval enforcement, automatic invalidation after edits, upload permission checks, destination visibility and provider read-back are not established by this inherited export bibliography or continuity supplement.

YouTube OAuth, privacyStatus and quota contracts are not applicable evidence for this Premiere-specific supplement and were not asserted; they require the separately assigned official YouTube research. No export, sharing or publication action was performed.

observed_facts: HISTORICAL BASELINE, October 20: The supplied artifact cites Adobe's keyboard-navigation and screen-reader/magnifier/operating-system support pages, plus panel navigation/docking documentation. Its adopted FrameForge choices include responsive native controls and focus preservation. These references and adoption choices are inherited, not fresh accessibility observations.

CURRENT CONTINUITY GAP: Saved workspace selection/reset documents layout restoration when handling multiple projects; it does not establish keyboard focus restoration, responsive mobile behavior or a WCAG conformance level.

PRE-BASELINE RELEASE DETAIL: Version 26.5.2 fixed Effect Controls values adjusted with Up/Down arrow keys not being retained. The fix predates October 20; no accessibility change during October 21-24 was established.
frameforge_implications: [INFERENCE] Preserve focus and selection through task/production switches, expose a keyboard route among bin, preview, timeline/graph and inspector, and provide explicit selected/read-only/missing/error status that does not rely on color alone.

[INFERENCE] Treat panel adaptation as progressive disclosure, not evidence that a desktop application's layout can simply shrink into a mobile viewport; verify FrameForge with keyboard and screen-reader scenarios separately.
limitations: [uncertain] Exact inherited shortcut mappings, assistive-technology coverage, focus retention, minimum screen dimensions and mobile adaptation cannot be recovered from the baseline's citation list alone and were intentionally not re-researched. No WCAG compliance, screen-reader success or responsive runtime result is claimed.
